examples.question_text:
Simplify these to unit rates. Give money rates to the nearest cent.
(a) $\$27.30$ for $3.5$ kg.
(b) $\$137$ for $6$ hours.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\frac{\$27.30}{3.5\text{ kg}}=\frac{\$7.80}{1\text{ kg}}=\$7.80\text{/kg}$.
Divide both quantities by $3.5$. This rate is exact.
(b) $\frac{\$137}{6\text{ h}}=\frac{\$22.8333\ldots}{1\text{ h}}\approx\$22.83\text{/h}$.
Divide both quantities by $6$, then round to the nearest cent.

(a) Kilometres go on top.
$\frac{154\text{ km}}{22\text{ L}}=\frac{7\text{ km}}{1\text{ L}}=7\text{ km/L}$.
(b) Litres go on top.
$\frac{22\text{ L}}{154\text{ km}}=\frac{\frac17\text{ L}}{1\text{ km}}=\frac17\text{ L/km}$.
The two rates are reciprocals. They describe the same journey with the quantities in a different order.

examples.question_text:
(a) A dentist sees $31$ patients between $9$ am and $4$ pm. Find the average rate in patients/hour, correct to $2$ decimal places.
(b) A seedling was $19$ cm tall on day $2$ and $58$ cm tall on day $8$. Find its average rate of growth per day.
examples.solution_text:
(a) From $9$ am to $4$ pm is $7$ hours.
$\frac{31\text{ patients}}{7\text{ h}}=\frac{4.428571\ldots\text{ patients}}{1\text{ h}}\approx4.43\text{ patients/h}$.
(b) Growth $=58-19=39$ cm.
Time $=8-2=6$ days.
$\frac{39\text{ cm}}{6\text{ days}}=\frac{6.5\text{ cm}}{1\text{ day}}=6.5\text{ cm/day}$.
Use the growth and the time between the two readings, not the final height and final day number.

examples.question_text: A car starts a $93$ km journey with a full $48$ L tank. At the end, the tank is two thirds full. Find the fuel consumption rate in kilometres per litre, correct to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Fuel left $=\frac23\times48=32$ L.
Fuel used $=48-32=16$ L.
$\frac{93\text{ km}}{16\text{ L}}=\frac{5.8125\text{ km}}{1\text{ L}}\approx5.81\text{ km/L}$.
Use the fuel consumed during the journey, not the fuel left in the tank.
